articleTitle: Designing a gateway IEEE1451-HL7 for E-health telemonitoring services
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: The development of devices to interconnect different technologies paves the way to achieve interoperability. Although E-health telemonitoring services have additional challenges to overcome, one of them is the semantic interoperability. The aim of this work is to shed light on that issue by proposing the design of a digital device handling the data of the sensors and sending it to the cloud. The device uses the connectivity standards IEEE802.15.4 and IEEE802.15.1 on the perception sub-layer and IEEE802.11 and IEEE802.3 for sending data to the cloud. Besides, the device will complaint the standards IEEE1451.0, IEEE1451.1, IEEE1451.5 and Health Level 7 (HL7) on the application layer. A block diagram description, block interrelationship, and circuit specifications is given. In addition, we include our customized hardware initial proposal with the tower K60F120, a Freescale developing board for embedded solutions. The conclusions include challenges and new directions about hardware options.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis sensors based on embedded system
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a microcontroller platform for real-time estimating reliability of sensors and electronic systems. Also we introduced a system using the smartphone for collecting real-time sensor data and simultaneously screen the data sensor on Android application, signals have been transmission using Bluetooth connections. This design is the advancement over ordinary wired sensor networks which are restricted to a fixed monitoring location. The proposed system minimize the deficiencies of the traditional reliability prediction methods for sensors or electronic systems like the use of generic failure rates for reliability prediction; and, the lack of realism of the reliability prediction in various operational environments. The key traits of the proposed methodology are its ability to incorporate all failure in real-time and dynamically modify the estimated reliability of the sensor or monitored system.

articleTitle: ON/OFF protocol for the life extension of low energy level nodes in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: WSNs are complex systems that are mainly limited by the battery life of the nodes in order to have an adequate performance. In most cases, it is possible to have a re-deployment of new nodes in order to prolong the system's lifetime. This leads to a situation where some nodes have a low energy level while other nodes have high energy levels. This scenario can also be found due to the use of a preferred route, where intermediate nodes consume more energy than the rest of the nodes. In these environments, and others, low energy nodes, i.e., nodes with very low residual energy must reduce the energy consumption since their operational lifetime is almost over. In this paper, we consider cluster-based WSNs for the event detection where there is a high concentration of high energy nodes and a low concentration of low energy nodes. Building on this, we propose to extend the battery life of low energy nodes in the steady stat phase. Specifically, we consider the case where nodes have random times in the sleep and active modes. To this end, we consider the case where dwelling times in each mode are related to the residual energy level. The system and the impact of the proposed residual energy-based mechanisms are evaluated and studied.

articleTitle: UHF RFID antennas integrated on flexible substrate for health care environments
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Most of RFID tags for radiofrequency identification applications are different among them since its design and fabrication process rely on intended application environment. Thus, RFID tag antennas should be made of materials suitable for its target application scenario allowing in the end, an efficient means for identification. In this paper, design and fabrication details of flexible RFID tags antennas is discussed, those tags were attached to a chip in order to measure the working area of the tags. Three prototypes of RFID antennas working in the UHF band of the spectrum were built by integrating it in Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate which is flexible, can be easily finished and resist most chemicals used for printed circuit board fabrication, that is why is widely used for making antennas.

articleTitle: Management of scientific and technological research
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Accessing the latest information of scientific and technological research projects and its results, is an essential requirement for the success in innovation. To provide the information access, Information Management Models are needed to promote innovation and improvement of existing research.

articleTitle: A flooding routing algorithm for a wireless sensor network for seismic events
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Lately the use of wireless sensor networks for monitoring seismic events has increased; however, these networks depends on the previous acknowledge of the infrastructure and topology. This topology can’t be updated if any of the nodes is lost during a seismic event, in addition the orientation of the first seismic wave can’t be predicted; because of this, it is necessary to use a type of dynamic network topology. Using ad hoc networks for this purpose could be the answer, but the routing algorithms used in these networks needs to fulfill some characteristics. This paper propose the implementation of a variant of flooding algorithm; evaluating its performance using OMNeT++ simulator; describing a scenario of a 24-floor building. The results are compared against a more commonly used protocol; proving the good performance of this variant and contributing to the state of art.

articleTitle: Optical character recognition based on phase features
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: A new method for recognition of content-less characters in low quality images using the phase congruency and local energy model is proposed. New phase features invariant to nonuniform illumination and slight geometric distortions are obtained. With the help of computer simulation the performance of the proposed method for character recognition in degraded images is presented and compared with that of common feature-based techniques in terms of recognition metrics.

articleTitle: A 910MHz/2.4GHz easily tunable dual-band antenna for power harvesting and sensor networking applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This work presents a 910MHz/2.4GHz dual-band dipole antenna for Power Harvesting and/or Sensor Network applications whose main advantage lies on its easily tunable bands. Tunability is achieved via the low and high frequency dipole separation W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gap</sub>. This separation is used to increase or decrease the S11 magnitude of the required bands. Such tunability can be used to harvest energy in environments where the electric field strength of one carrier band is dominant over the other one, or in the case when both carriers have similar electric field strength. If the environment is crowed by 820MHz-1.02GHz carries W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gap</sub> is adjusted to 1mm in order to harvest/sense only the selected band; if the environment is full of 2.24GHz - 2.52 GHz carriers W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gap</sub> is set to 7mm. When W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gap</sub> is selected to 4mm both bands can be harvested/sensed. The proposed antenna works for UHF-RFID, GSM-840MHz, 3G-UMTS, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth standards. Simulations are carried out in Advanced Design System (ADS) Momentum using commercial FR4 printed circuit board specification.

articleTitle: Digital architecture to implement a piecewise-linear approximation for the hyperbolic tangent function
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: In this paper an 8 bits word-length digital architecture that implements a piecewise-linear approximation for the hyperbolic tangent function is presented. Among the main characteristics of this architecture, it can be highlighted its low memory consumption (only two data breakpoints are considered for function approximation), and its hardware portability because it can be implemented in a wide variety of programmable devices like FPGA, DSP or microcontrollers. In order to verify the feasibility of this proposal, logic circuit simulations in Proteus as well as numerical simulations in Maple, are reported.

articleTitle: Design of an advanced telemetry mission using CanSat
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This work is the first step of developing a Nanosatellite, the fundamental mission of the system is the collection of telemetry data in the Veracruz-Boca del Rio, with special emphasis on measuring air pollutants, the typical measured variables are temperature, relative air pressure, relative humidity, altitude, and position, the development of the system architecture consists of a flight segment and ground station, which show data through a desktop interface variables measured in real time and stored for later analysis. The proposed project is a prototype based in the course on space systems engineering, which was held in December 2014 in collaboration with the Mexican space agency.

articleTitle: A sensor network to obtain real-time rain-attenuation
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: To obtain the attenuation level in links at frequencies higher than 10 Ghz, rain is the most important factor to consider. In spite of the existence of statistical models to calculate the rain attenuation -such as ITU-R standards- sometimes it is necessary to have an approximation to real-time rain-attenuation in the link. In this paper a sensor network that monitors the rain rate of different regions in México has been developed; the collected data are used to obtain rain attenuation values. In this work, the design of the network as well as a Graphical User Interface (GUI) and a database to store the data collected is explained.

articleTitle: A system for capture, transmission and mix digital audio
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: The objective of this work is to explain the development of a functional system for live audio. The system can manage the information without considerable delays of time and it can mix channels from different sources. The system has an audio console emulated in the computer, it means an improve in mobility and less weight. The signal processing of each channel is done within the console, so you can equalize it. The captured information by the system is sent to the console by a local area network, in the console the signal is mixed and finally sent to the exit points of audio.

articleTitle: Developing of a practical teaching method of digital terrestrial television based on software
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Communications and transmissions tend increasingly to be digital, because of this television signals are leaving transmit with analog standards. For this reason, it is important to teach and analyze the necessary information to implement the Digital Terrestrial Television (DTT). In this case we are going to focus on the ATSC (Advance Television System Committee) standard, which is what Mexico has adopted. The aim of this article is to present a new method of practical teaching for the Radio-communication area in general and particularly the matter "Digital Television" so the student can understand and analyze the different stages of coding, modulation, transmission and reception of the Digital Terrestrial Television (DTT) through Software Defined Radio (SDR). To develop Software Defined Radio (SDR) and follow the trend towards digital transmissions, there are some devices that implement various communication protocols, including UMTS, GSM, WIFI, Bluetooth, etc. With this we have been developed projects of free software such as GNU Radio and USRP software. GNU Radio can operate as a Simulator or with the computer sound card.

articleTitle: Study of failures in interconnection wires between basic digital gates
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Some of the flaws in the interconnection wires of digital integrated circuits can be caused by fabrication defects or wear as the effect of electromigration effect. Interconnection wires add parasitic effects such as resistances and capacitances which contribute to the propagation delay of a logic gate signal to another. For long length wires the Elmore delay model for RC networks ladder, allows to estimate the propagation delay of a wire ideally without faults, and give a vision of the repercussions in the output signal between two connected inverters with a faulty wire at different points. Therefore, is presented a study of propagation delay in interconnection wire for a TSMC 0.18μm technology.

articleTitle: An optimized collaborative platform for educational cloud computing in application and presentation layers of OSI model
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: In this paper we will talk about an approach for online course publishing that has not been exploited totally, the creation of an education platform using cloud computing. This approach allows to see a new tool for its use as innovative educational technology. In the first instance, the rapid growth of social networks has proposed a tendency to create collaborative spaces, with no educational purposes, being the most common leisure and informative for its use. On appeal, cloud computing in recent years has demonstrated to have benefits that were not given with the traditional distribution of contents through the internet, it also allows to distribute information on distinct servers in distinct geographical areas, and having this way a system that is always available with no delays on content delivery.

articleTitle: Global model MOHYSE, a new tool to assess the effect of hydro-meteorological phenomena in the tropics
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: In this research the adaptation to tropical conditions of a Canadian global hydrological model (GHM) called MOHYSE was performed, and the efficiency of its hydrological response was evaluated. A hydrological modeling study over central watersheds of the Gulf of Mexico was performed and various indices were calculated to evaluate the GHM response. Additionally, the GHM was compared with a semi-distributed hydrological model (SDHM) to determine which of the models was closest to the hydrograph observed in the study area. The results indicate that both models adequately fit to tropical conditions; however the MOHYSE obtained better results in the statistical analysis compared to the SDHM, mainly with the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency coefficient. Likewise, these results have direct application in the analysis of flood risk areas and could serve as an useful tool for policy makers.

articleTitle: Social networks: generating opportunities for organizations and users in Mexico
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Social networks in Mexico have higher levels of ownership by users despite the eminent digital divide. There are three most popular and important social networks: Facebook, Twitter and YouTube, each has different characteristics that identifies but by using these parts of the organization is now a need to maintain a healthy and constant communication. In this paper a documentary analysis of the advantages of use with these social networks from the perspective of organizations and users is performed. The result of the research is the synthesis of these advantages presented in comparative tables allowing clarify their use and appropriation.

articleTitle: Deploying agents assistance collaborative communities
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: Currently a predominant need for organizations is the support service that can provide its customers and partners, this assistance is an issue of great importance for the value involving customers and pays off in image for the organization. Thus the investment to sustain this service you get to become significant figures that could be saved by implementing Agents Assistance (AA) based software, which are always available to customers in most cases solve the most common problems users. The significantly lower investment for companies and an image is projected technological domain. It is for this reason that in this paper an architecture for implementing agents Assistance is defined, it explains an overview of the architecture design and implementation in different environments looking that can be integrated in collaborative environments which allow increasing knowledge and ability to service agents.

articleTitle: Security vulnerabilities of the Mexican digital invoices by internet
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This paper presents a security analysis of the Mexican digital invoices by Internet. The paper discusses the state-of-the-art of the main cryptographic standards used for generating the digital invoices, and points out their vulnerabilities, finally some recommendations are presented.

articleTitle: REMMA citizen observatory: a monitoring and an alerting real-time system
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This paper proposes a prototype for real-time monitoring and alerting when weather or air pollution is above the international thresholds. This prototype keeps end user informed via a web application where user can check historic data and via a mobile application where user can check the alarm system. Each micro-station could be installed at any part of Mexican soil or it can be reconfigured without stopping the entire system and without user intervention. The station will auto-configure looking for database servers to send data acquired, it will auto-heal when sensors are out of range preventing from fill the database with false data and it will autooptimize when there is a black-out or low energy situation. The station has been tested only with controlled laboratory test but a long run test is still needs to be done.

articleTitle: Parallel and numerical issues of the edge finite element method for 3D controlled-source electromagnetic surveys
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This paper deals with the most relevant parallel and numerical issues that arise when applying the Edge Element Method in the solution of electromagnetic problems in exploration geophysics. In this sense, in recent years the application of land and marine controlled-source electromagnetic (CSEM) surveys has gained tremendous interest among the offshore exploration community. This method is especially significant in detecting hydrocarbon in shallow/deep waters. On the other hand, in Finite Element Methods for solving electromagnetic field problems, the use of Edge Elements has become very popular. In fact, Edge Elements are often said to be a cure to many difficulties that are encountered (particularly eliminating spurious solutions) and are claimed to yield accurate results. CSEM, linear vectorial edge basis functions and its implementation on unstructured tetrahedral meshes are discussed. The use of it's kind of discretisation enables the representation of complex geological structures and allows local refinement in order to improve the solution's accuracy. A parallel shared memory approach is proposed to meet the high computational cost of EM modeling. Performance results and an convergence study are presented in order to validate our numerical method.

articleTitle: The development of a software architecture for an environmental education platform
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: With time, software systems have become increasingly complex. It is not enough to think about software complexity in terms of algorithms and data structures. It has become necessary to think about software architecture. This work presents the development of a software architecture for a environmental education platform. Such an environmental education and communication platform is being developed in order to attend the needs of sensitizing people towards climate change. It has been appreciated that current practices for climate change awareness are not enough and that new strategies are needed. In order to this, it has been proposed to develop an environmental education platform. Such a platform requires, as its main resource, a software architecture. The development of the software architecture for the education environmental platform is presented.

articleTitle: Usability test of a SCADA system for monitoring and operating an experimental wind rotor
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Computing Systems and Telematics (ICCSAT)
abstract: This paper presents the tracking of the usability test "Thinking Aloud" of a SCADA system for monitoring and operating a wind rotor (BEPA), which is coupled to an experimental prototype rotor. Consequently, it was necessary to define the user profile of the candidates to the test, and the creation of 9 usability tasks. While performing the tests, 3 potential users were involved and 18 usability problems were found that were treated by priority, therefore, it was achieved to have a first impression of the usability of BEPA against the user perception concerning their mental model, offering positive results for continuous improvement of the system.
